title: Carbon Cycle and Greenhouse Gases
text: The carbon cycle describes the exchange of carbon among the atmosphere, oceans, land, and living organisms. Carbon dioxide (CO2) is removed from the atmosphere through photosynthesis by plants and algae, and by absorption in the oceans. It is released back through cellular respiration, decomposition, volcanic eruptions, and burning of fossil fuels. The ocean absorbs approximately 25–30% of human CO2 emissions, though this is causing acidification. Methane (CH4), produced by cattle, rice paddies, landfills, and natural gas leaks, is about 80 times more potent as a greenhouse gas than CO2 over 20 years but has a shorter atmospheric lifetime. The current atmospheric CO2 concentration of over 420 ppm is the highest in at least 3 million years.
